clue.text: Dreadfully slay with a cut, producing this?

definitions.text: Dreadfully slay with a cut, producing this?

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters of the words are thrown into a new and terrible order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim question about what a vicious slash leaves behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: savagely slaying someone with a cut produces exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim of violence or an accident, the result of a deadly cut, is called by this word.

clue.text: Party drink I had for boy with amorous aims

parts.note: a cup is a mixed punch-like drink served at parties
contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a drink at a party they had with a lad who fancied them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is a boy archer whose arrows make people fall in love.

clue.text: Oil finally framed by excited artist, like nativity scene

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the other piece as a picture sits in a frame
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the word itself supplies the letters to be jumbled

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: its last letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: An agitated painter adds a last touch of oil to a Christmas crib picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The stable at Bethlehem is pictured under the bright star, so the scene is lit by stars.

clue.text: Part of curve discernible in bar chart

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of bar and start of chart run together to hold the answer

explanation.surface: A curved segment shows up in a statistical graph.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment of a circle's circumference is the geometric term meant.

clue.text: Freely include argument swallowed by lightweight

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other, as food is swallowed

parts.note: thin, slight in build
a row, a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A puny fellow gulps down a quarrel and lets something in for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something as a free extra to a deal is to give it gratis.

clue.text: Rhythmic performer providing rhyme for answer (and the next one)

definitions.meaning: the plain sense: someone who moves to a beat on stage

definitions.text: providing rhyme for answer (and the next one)
definitions.meaning: the setter's joke: this reindeer's name rhymes with the word answer and with the name in the next clue

explanation.surface: A performer who keeps time also happens to rhyme with two words.
explanation.walkthrough: The next clue gives Prancer, and both rhyme with answer; the two are paired in the list of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moves rhythmically to music is a performer of steps, and is also one of Santa's reindeer.

clue.text: 3 disheartened and upset in African capital

indicators.note: with its heart, the middle letter, taken out

parts.note: the answer to clue 3, a part of a curve, used for both halves

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: the same answer to clue 3, this time turned around

explanation.surface: Someone is dispirited and distressed in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 3 is used twice: once without its middle letter and once reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana's capital city lies on the Gulf of Guinea coast in West Africa.

clue.text: It's difficult to assemble without one vote

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: compile, gather into a collection
I, the Roman numeral
an X is the cross put on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A complaint that putting something together without a single vote is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate with many interlinked parts is hard to understand or deal with.

clue.text: Denser ice fashioned into igloo, for example

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped, so the letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: the two words supply exactly the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Compacted ice blocks are shaped into a snow house.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dwelling, a home where someone lives.

clue.text: Some interlopers I accosted in home of 27, originally

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the words that follow are wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of interlopers, the I and the start of accosted

explanation.surface: Someone confronted a few intruders.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 27 is the wise men, traditionally thought to have come from the old name for Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient empire now called Iran is thought to be where the Magi set out from.

clue.text: Lively horse, after quiet start, sprinted — almost sure winner

parts.note: ran fast, the past tense of the verb

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a cert is a certainty, a horse sure to win

explanation.surface: A racing tip: a frisky horse that ran well after a quiet start is nearly a certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: A cert, short for certainty, is British racing slang for a horse sure to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that prances is high-spirited and frisky, and the name belongs to one of Santa's reindeer.

clue.text: Teenager's complaint rejected by politicians — sets up temporary site

indicators.note: rejected as in thrown back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: acne, the skin complaint typical of adolescence
MPs, Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: A teenager's grievance is dismissed by politicians, who then pitch a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The complaint is a medical one, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To camp is to set up a temporary base or site, as soldiers or travellers do.

clue.text: Kind of wings with which Daedalus began

definitions.meaning: first meaning: triangular swept-back aircraft wings
second meaning: the NATO alphabet word for the letter D, which starts the name Daedalus

explanation.walkthrough: Daedalus, who made wings for himself and Icarus, makes the wings seem mythical; the second sense is only his initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangular aircraft wings share their name with the Greek letter and radio code word for D.

clue.text: A small collection that's valuable to owner

parts.note: taken as written
a set, a group of things that belong together

explanation.surface: A modest assembly of items prized by whoever holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of value owned by a person or company is a resource counted in its favour.

clue.text: Celebrated at Christmas, criticised by wife at first

indicators.note: the wife comes first, at the front of the other piece

parts.note: assailed, attacked with words

explanation.surface: Someone's Christmas revels are attacked by their wife from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To wassail is to go carolling and drinking festive toasts, an old way of celebrating Yuletide.

clue.text: Flier for cricket club

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the wooden implement a cricketer strikes the ball with

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket club reads like a sports team; here it is the striking implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a nocturnal winged mammal and the wooden striking implement used in cricket.

clue.text: Support seen romantically and made effective, retrospectively

parts.note: back, as in endorse
dated, went out with as a partner

explanation.surface: Someone supported and courted, with the relationship counted from earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A document marked with an earlier date takes effect from a time already past.

clue.text: Jovial old man assault can upset

indicators.note: upset as in knocked over and disarranged, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful elderly man can be upset by an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is traditionally pictured as a merry, bearded old gentleman.

clue.text: Earth mother?

definitions.meaning: reads as a nurturing goddess figure or motherly woman
flags that earth is a fox's burrow, so the mother is a female fox

explanation.walkthrough: A fox's den is called an earth, so the mother who lives in one is a female fox.
explanation.definitionFit: The female fox, who raises cubs in an underground den, has this name, also borne by a reindeer.

clue.text: Short stay, very short — that so?

parts.note: V is the short form of very
'is it?', the reply that means 'is that so?'

explanation.surface: A doubtful response to a brief stay being very brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling on someone briefly, or a stay of limited length, is this noun.

clue.text: Arrive ahead of time as celestial omen?

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the second

parts.note: come, as in reach a place

explanation.surface: Turning up early as a sign from the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright tailed body in the sky was long taken as a portent; one of Santa's reindeer shares the name.

clue.text: Writing about incense in eating places, one of which had another role at Christmas

definitions.text: eating places, one of which had another role at Christmas

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: MS, short for manuscript
as a verb, incense means enrage; here the noun anger

explanation.surface: Manuscripts on burning incense in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Incense is not the scented smoke but the verb to enrage. The infant Jesus was laid in a feeding trough.
explanation.definitionFit: Troughs that animals eat from are feeding places; one served as the crib at Bethlehem.

clue.text: See 16
Brainboxes operated in intelligence group

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the CIA, the US Central Intelligence Agency
ran, as in managed or worked

explanation.surface: Clever people working in a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Brainboxes suggests clever people; here it means the bony boxes holding the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulls are the bony cases that enclose the brain, literally boxes for brains.

clue.text: Bail due, as arranged within hearing

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the two words supply exactly the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bail is set in court within earshot, as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be heard is loud enough to reach the ears.

clue.text: Female of 31, say, finishes off crossword so simple

indicators.note: the finishing letters of each of the following words are taken

parts.note: the last letters of the three words, one from each

explanation.surface: A boast that the crossword is easily wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 31 gives the animals pulling Santa's sleigh; the female of that kind of deer is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of a deer, including a reindeer, is called by this short word.

clue.text: Repeatedly, unknown learner is falling in awful ride — not heavy fall

indicators.note: falling in says these letters drop inside the rearranged word
awful means terrible, so the letters of ride are rearranged
repeatedly says the unknown letter appears twice

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: A beginner keeps falling off during a dreadful ride, though the weather is only light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns RIDE into DRIE; 'Repeatedly' doubles Z, and ZZL goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drizzle is fine light rain, the opposite of a heavy downpour.

clue.text: Tempestuous duo completing 16's team of 31

definitions.meaning: the names mean thunder and lightning in German, a stormy pair
they are the last two named in the list of Santa Claus's reindeer

explanation.walkthrough: In German, Donner is thunder and Blitz is lightning; the pair close the roll call in 'A Visit from St Nicholas'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final two of Santa's eight reindeer in the classic poem bear German names for a storm's thunder and lightning.

clue.text: European story gets uplifting treatment to fill with joy

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means lifted upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a tale

explanation.surface: A European story is upbeat enough to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone elated is to raise their spirits greatly.

clue.text: Group of travellers in next answer, for example, held back in congested air traffic

definitions.text: Group of travellers in next answer, for example

indicators.note: held back as in turned back, so the hidden letters read from right to left
the letters sit inside the run of words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of congested, all of air and the start of traffic

explanation.surface: Travellers are delayed in a crowded sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The next answer is the three wise men, a group of three travellers following the star.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three is a trio, and the wise men who journeyed to Bethlehem are such a set.

clue.text: Person who gives fellow gold

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A man who donates gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who donates money or blood is a benefactor or contributor.

clue.text: Those giving truly original Christmas presents

definitions.meaning: seems to describe inventive modern gift buyers
original in the sense of first: they brought the very first Christmas gifts

explanation.walkthrough: Original here means first, not inventive: the wise men gave gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men of the Nativity story brought the first gifts to the newborn Jesus.

clue.text: See 23
Occupying, we hear, accommodation full at Christmas

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: in, as in occupying a place

explanation.surface: We hear the lodgings are booked solid over Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: At Bethlehem there was no room at the inn for Mary and Joseph.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub with rooms to let offers lodging; the Bethlehem one famously had no vacancy.

clue.text: Fast mover, as found in herd, possibly

indicators.note: signals that these letters may form another word if rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A speedy animal turns up among the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in herd' suggests a hidden word, but the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rushes about is one who moves at speed; the name also belongs to a reindeer.

clue.text: Soundly control beloved animals

explanation.walkthrough: The first word is spelt as it means; only the second changes spelling when heard.
